Adding a digital version of your driver's license to your iPhone will soon be available in the 15th US state.

Apple currently lists 14 states that support the feature, as well as the territory of Puerto Rico, but backend assets suggest another state will be added soon……

Many of us have long hoped for a future where we no longer need to carry physical identification documents such as driver's licenses and passports, but can simply present digital ID via iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future still seems a long way off, but Apple took its first step back in 2021, when it announced plans to allow iPhone users to add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. To date, 14 states have adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend assets discovered by MacRumors indicate that Oklahoma will soon join this list.

We previously provided a detailed guide on how to add your driver's license or state ID to your iPhone's Wallet app. At that time, we also reminded everyone that digital IDs cannot completely replace physical documents, so you still need to continue carrying the physical version.

That said, the digital version can still help protect your privacy at qualified TSA checkpoints and when you need to prove your age to a merchant. The ID will confirm that you meet the age requirement without disclosing any personal information, such as your date of birth.
